subject: Re: RetailCo \u0014 Post-call recap & model fit evaluation (quality regression concern)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@retailco.com>
Cc: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@retailco.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: RetailCo kickoff  post-call recap + next steps

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today  great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery focused on model fit and quality for your customer support summarization use case: 

Summary of needs:
- High factuality on short summaries (<= 2 sentences) for customer tickets
- Preserve sensitive PII redaction rules you described (email/phone removal)
- Strict SLO for latency (~200ms p50 for single-thread summaries) because you'll be embedding into a live agent UI

Recommended model/profile to try:
- Redwood-qa-1.3 (quantized)  balances cost and factuality, our internal retail benchmark shows lowest hallucination rate on ticket summaries.
- Fallback: Redwood-qa-1.2 (non-quantized) if you need slightly higher strictness on exact-match fields.

Links and assets I promised:
- Benchmark results + evaluation prompt sets: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bBenchmarkRetailCo
- Prompt deck (examples + guardrails) included in the folder

Next steps (proposed):
1) We provision a short POC with Redwood-qa-1.3 for 48 hours and push a curated prompt set (I can drop the starter prompts into your sandbox).
2) You run 100 ticket evals using your worst-case prompt set; we collect logs and surface a diff report.
3) If there are quality regressions we'll either pin to a prior model version or coordinate a rollback while we investigate root cause.

Can you confirm you're ok with that cadence? If yes I'll spin up the POC and loop in our infra engineer to handle pinning/rollback options you asked about.

Thanks 
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
https://redwood.ai

Attachment: sample-output-examples.txt (3 examples of current production outputs vs. expected)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear plan  that works. Quick heads up: we had a model update last week (your hosted endpoint moved from redwood-qa-1.2 -> redwood-qa-1.3 automatically) and since then our internal QA started seeing an increase in missing key facts in summaries for the returns flow. I attached a short set of examples in the drive but want to flag it now because our PM is sensitive to regressions.

We're happy to proceed with the POC you suggested, but before spinning up anything new can you: 
- Confirm whether pinning to 1.2 is an option for our workspace immediately (we need a short-term stopgap)
- Share what diffs you can quickly surface between v1.2 and v1.3 so we can triage impact areas

Thanks  appreciate the quick turnaround.

Samantha

Subject: Re: RetailCo kickoff  post-call recap + next steps

Samantha  thanks for flagging. Looping in Nikhil (infra/serving) and Rishi (Customer Success) to detail pin/rollback options and a quick diff summary.

Nikhil / Rishi  RetailCo saw quality shifts after the hosted update to redwood-qa-1.3. They've attached examples in the shared Drive (link above). Can you confirm:
1) Fastest way to pin their workspace to 1.2 / or pin only the production route?
2) What immediate diffs we can share (top regressions by intent/slot) and whether there's a known rollout change that could explain behaviour (tokenization change, temperature default, or spec tweak)?

I think for T-0 we should give the customer the ability to pin while we investigate; please advise timing.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha@retailco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@retailco.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RetailCo kickoff  post-call recap + next steps

Hi all  quick update after a first-pass triage. I pulled the evaluation logs Marissa uploaded and ran a diff against the 100-ticket sample. Summary: 

Findings (top-level):
- redwood-qa-1.3 shows a 12% increase in omitted entities for the "returns" intent versus 1.2 on your sample (see attached retailco_eval_diffs_20270804.csv).
- No tokenization changes between releases; the primary changes were a small decoding parameter tweak and a revised persona-conditioning prompt baked into the hosted route. That persona conditioning appears to be the likely culprit for the factuality shift.

Immediate mitigation options:
A) Pin workspace to redwood-qa-1.2  fastest (we can flip at the workspace routing level in ~30 minutes).
B) Pin only production route to 1.2 while leaving dev/staging on 1.3  takes ~45 minutes and preserves their ability to test newer behavior.
C) Apply a temporary prompt override (we can push a guardrail prompt)  near-immediate but requires eval to ensure latency SLO stays intact.

Recommended path: option B (pin production route to 1.2). It gives RetailCo immediate stability while preserving dev testing. I attached a short instruction set (model-v1.3-pinning-instructions.pdf) and included a small set of sample-output-examples.txt for quick verification.

If you'd like, I can schedule the pinning for today at 10:30am PT; it's a non-disruptive routing change. If you prefer the dev team to approve first, we can wait.

Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.ai

Can you confirm the rollback/pin will preserve our request logs and that we can unpin at any time? Also, can you share a short acceptance checklist we should run after the flip?

Samantha
